exposure: History of at least one successful vaginal delivery
cohort: The study included 236 class III obese women (BMI ≥ 40) aged 18 or older with a singleton, cephalic pregnancy attempting vaginal delivery after 24 weeks.
finding: Preeclampsia was associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery (adjusted OR 4.08), while a history of previous successful vaginal delivery was a protective factor (adjusted OR 0.20) in class III obese women attempting vaginal birth.
mod_finding: Preeclampsia increased the likelihood of cesarean delivery, whereas a history of successful vaginal delivery reduced this risk for class III obese women attempting vaginal birth.
